findings.text: Rule 9 sent every bare specifier it did not claim to "external", so an alias from an unread tsconfig disappeared and the report could say a bare "no cycles found". A bare specifier is now external only when it is a declared dependency or a Node.js built-in; any other goes on the could-not-resolve list, and an import into an excluded file is listed with "target excluded". Validator correction 3 names every reason the list now holds. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-7 and f-s6-agent-r1-17.

The alias algorithm was three vague lines with no reading rule, no extends and no precedence. It is now an exact procedure: nearest tsconfig or jsconfig, comments and trailing commas removed outside strings (the file's own choice), extends followed, TypeScript's longest-prefix precedence, and anything unread sent to the could-not-resolve list. Corrections 4, 5 and 6: paths and baseUrl are taken from the nearest file that sets each; the extends rule now cites TypeScript's own extends page; an alias that is itself a declared dependency or built-in stays external.

A C# using inside a namespace was matched literally and lost as external, and the namespace shapes were undefined. The directive is now looked up from the enclosing namespace outward (labelled the file's reading, not checked against a compiler), and the node a using comes from, nested blocks and the global namespace are defined. Corrects f-s6-agent-r2-8.

The madge recipes passed a cycle that closes through a tsconfig alias (session run 1), never read four extensions (run 2), and called themselves fail-closed too broadly. They now pass --ts-config only when a root tsconfig.json exists: the critic's unconditional form stopped every commit in a project without one (session section 5), so the GitHub Actions step takes the validator's three-line conditional and the pre-commit hook the session's TSCONFIG block and command lines byte for byte (pre-commit-r3b.sh). The prose states what the recipes still miss and that madge@8 is a range. Correction 1 replaced the untested "delete that option" sentence with the runs; correction 2 cites madge's tsConfig option. At the session's direction the status sentence also names the sixth run: a tsconfig.json with comments and trailing commas is read by madge 8.0.0. The hook was run by the session in five states, and the command the hook prints for details in a sixth (the executor's first wording, "the hook's madge command ... as tsc --init writes it", named the wrong command and carried an unsourced phrase; the re-read's pair 8 corrected both, finding f-s6-agent-r3-21); the GitHub Actions step was not run. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-10 and f-s6-agent-r2-4.

findings.text: A module whose imports were never resolved (every Go, Rust and PHP module) was reported as "isolated". It is now "instability not known - N imports could not be resolved", other isolated modules are qualified when the list is not empty, and modules with an unresolved import are marked in the coupling table. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-4.

Rule 1 claimed TypeScript's substitution order but reversed it (session run 3, raw), and letter case could split one file into two nodes. The substitutions now come before the path as written, declaration files are skipped as the file's own choice, and candidates are compared with the directory listing. Correction 12: a type-only import that only a declaration file answers gives a type-only edge. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-7, whose validator leftover 2 wrote the rule 1 wording.

exports conditions had no defined fallback, pattern keys were not handled, and "main" was used for subpaths exports hides. Pattern keys and nested conditions are handled, the fallback key order is defined as the file's own pick, an unexported subpath goes on the could-not-resolve list as "not exported", and rule 3 reads imports the same way. Corrections 13 and 14: the longest matching pattern key wins, and the fallback looks inside nested objects. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-16.

Python namespace packages and second source roots were not handled, and the parent-package rule was uncited. A namespace package gives no edge, an absolute import matching a scanned name outside the source root is listed rather than external, and section 5.2.1 is cited (read raw by the session). Correction 11 keeps a subpackage such as src/app/logging/ from catching `import logging`. Corrects f-s6-agent-r2-9.

The Java unnamed package had no node, and only C# was called a lower bound. The unnamed-package node is named, citing the Java Language Specification section 7.4.2, and the Java graph is a lower bound too, including packages that only excluded generated sources declare. Corrects f-s6-agent-r2-8.

findings.text: "One script" contradicted the separate Python part, and nothing governed symbolic links or how the script gets its file list. The script now lists files itself, follows no symbolic link, and reports skipped links and any difference from Step 1's count. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-7.

findings.text: Whether an import inside a branch counts was left to inference. The script evaluates no condition apart from Python's TYPE_CHECKING rule.

Nothing covered scale or cut output, a false green on large repositories. The script uses an iterative component search (the file's own choice), prints the number of files read, ends with "records printed: N", and never reports from cut output. Correction 9: a middle cut is caught by comparing N with the lines received, and each re-run section ends with its own count. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-13.

A root manifest or a src/index.ts collapsed every file into one module, and modules were keyed by name. The repository root and the source root are never module boundaries by themselves, and modules are keyed by repository-relative path. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-19.

The architecture checker's rules file went unmentioned, and allowedCycles entries could silently never match. The header now discloses .ctoc/architecture-rules.yaml and that the checker's verdicts can differ; which file governs both agents is put to the human; allowedCycles entries are normalised, glob entries match nothing, and unmatched entries are listed. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-12.

MITRE classes CWE-1047 and CWE-1054 as quality issues with no direct security implications (status "Incomplete", mapping usage "Prohibited"), so the file now says never to present a cycle or layer violation as a security weakness; CWE-1047's Java sentence backs the package graph and CWE-1054's vertical-utility sentence backs the defaults for utils only.

The report template had no place for items the text promises. The Limits block gains slots for files with no layer, ignorePaths patterns, unmatched allowedCycles entries, unreadable tsconfig files, skipped symbolic links, letter case and graph lower bounds; an accepted-cycles section and a low-severity cycle row are added. Corrections 7 and 8: the tsconfig slot covers extends targets and files not found, and the lower-bound slot is added. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-11.

findings.text: Comparison Mode graded cycles as new or unchanged with no matching rule, against the Role. It now states the presence check and an exact-node-set matching rule as the file's own, and leaves the verdict to quality/architecture-checker. Correction 10: a grown component is not also listed as resolved, layer and stable-dependencies violations get their own matching rules, and the Role is reconciled explicitly. Corrects f-s6-agent-r1-14.

Which rules file governs layers when both .dependency-rules.json and .ctoc/architecture-rules.yaml exist: the two use different schemas and give opposite verdicts on a controller importing a model. Finding 14 only discloses the second file; the choice spans two agents.

The structured output schema and a confidence per finding: for the third consecutive round the critic caps Integration on their absence, so under its escalation rule ("same issue three rounds") it goes to the dispatcher as a design question about how the wrapper is structured.

findings.text: The re-read of the round-3 file found every pair and correction landed, every quotation verified and both hook blocks equal to the tested bytes, and left eight pairs, all applied: pair 8 corrects the sixth-run sentence, which named the hook's counting command although the session ran the command the hook prints for details (no --json), and called the commented tsconfig.json "as tsc --init writes it", a phrase no source backs (the session wrote that file by hand); pairs 2 to 4 give the Incremental Analysis table full module keys, as finding 13 requires; pairs 5 and 6 add template slots for modules whose instability is not known and for languages whose imports were extracted but not resolved; pair 7 names "the algorithm's step 2" so it is not read as Step 2; pair 1 (optional, taken) gives the first could-not-resolve category its reason, "no such file". Corrects f-s6-agent-r3-1 (pair 1), -2 (pair 7), -4 (pair 8), -5 (pair 5), -13 (pairs 2 to 4) and -16 (pair 6).

seven_languages.reason: The domain applies to all seven languages, because each has an import or include mechanism. Analysed: TypeScript and JavaScript, Python, Java and C#; this round fixes TypeScript and JavaScript bare specifiers, aliases, exports, substitution order and letter case, Python namespace packages and second source roots, the Java unnamed package and lower bound, and C# namespace lookup and shapes. Extracted but unresolved: Go, Rust and PHP, every import on the could-not-resolve list, their modules now reading "instability not known" instead of the false "isolated". Detected but not analysed: C, C++ and SQL (Step 1); no round-3 source gives a verified rule for them. No new code example in any language. The Java and C# rules are not compiled: there is no JDK and no .NET on this machine.
